direct_answer: Evidence on whether creatine improves grip strength in older adults is mixed [C1, C3].
synthesis:
A small randomized trial found that grip strength increased by 2.1 kg with creatine versus 0.4 kg with placebo after 12 weeks [C1]. In contrast, a cohort study found no association between creatine use and grip strength [C3].

A systematic review of nine trials in adults of all ages reported higher upper-body strength with creatine, which is only indirect evidence for older adults [C4].

evidence_rows.finding: Grip strength +2.1 kg with creatine vs +0.4 kg with placebo at 12 weeks
No association with grip strength (difference 0.2 kg)
Higher upper-body strength across nine trials in all ages

rating.justification: One small trial and one cohort disagree, and the review is indirect.
